body.statement: At \(P=P^{\diamond}\), the declared objects satisfy \(X_0=\{-1/2,1/2\}\), \(H=\{(-1/2,1/2),(1/2,-1/2)\}\), \(g=0\), \(A=1/2\), \(T=0\), and \(\nu_P=\tfrac12\delta_{-1/2}-\tfrac12\delta_{1/2}\). The obstacle endpoints are \(\ell_P(-1/2)=\ell_P(1/2)=-1/2\) and \(r_P(-1/2)=r_P(1/2)=1/2\), so \(\mathcal C_P=\{u:|u(-1/2)|\le1/2,\ |u(1/2)|\le1/2\}\) and \(\Theta(P)=[-1,1]\). For every such \(u\), the displayed schedules of \(Q_u^{\diamond}\) preserve \(P^{\diamond}\), satisfy \(|b_u^{\diamond}|\le1\), obey parallel trends on the baseline-treatment support and, because their period difference is \(u(X)\) at every dose, also obey the stronger all-\(I\) equality, have \(m_{Q_u^{\diamond}}=u\), and attain \(\theta(Q_u^{\diamond})=u(1/2)-u(-1/2)\). The endpoint assignment \(u(-1/2)=1/2,u(1/2)=-1/2\) gives \(b_u^{\diamond}=-1\) and \(\theta(Q_u^{\diamond})=-1\); reversing the two signs gives \(b_u^{\diamond}=1\) and \(\theta(Q_u^{\diamond})=1\). This is a heterogeneous two-point baseline design with both signs of treatment change, not the common-zero-baseline scalar design.
body.justification: The calculation makes the non-singleton frontier and its full-law attainment visible in the smallest genuinely heterogeneous-baseline design.
body.gap: The common-zero-baseline bounded-slope interval in de Chaisemartin et al. (2024) has one baseline and one scalar nuisance; this example has two baselines, opposite change signs, a signed objective, and distinct affine completions.
body.consumer: The worked law is a unit test for endpoint software and a transparent template for explaining support-driven partial identification in applications.
body.proof_tex:
Under \(P^{\diamond}\), the two atoms give
\[
(X,Z)=(-1/2,1/2)
\quad\text{and}\quad
(X,Z)=(1/2,-1/2),
\]
each with probability \(1/2\).  Therefore
\[
X_0=\{-1/2,1/2\},
\qquad
H=\{(-1/2,1/2),(1/2,-1/2)\}.
\]
Because \(Y_1=Y_2=0\) at both atoms, \(\Delta Y=0\), the support version of the conditional mean is \(g=0\), and \(T=0\).  Moreover,
\[
A=E_{P^{\diamond}}|Z|=\frac12,
\qquad
\nu_{P^{\diamond}}
=\frac12\delta_{-1/2}-\frac12\delta_{1/2}.
\]

With \(K=L=M=1\), direct substitution in the obstacle definitions gives, at either baseline, the local bounds \([-1/2,1/2]\).  The cone transported from the other baseline is weaker because the baselines are distance one apart.  Hence
\[
\ell_{P^{\diamond}}(-1/2)=\ell_{P^{\diamond}}(1/2)=-\frac12,
\qquad
r_{P^{\diamond}}(-1/2)=r_{P^{\diamond}}(1/2)=\frac12.
\]
Any two numbers in these intervals differ by at most one, so the one-Lipschitz constraint imposes no additional restriction.  The obstacle-compatibility theorem therefore gives
\[
\mathcal C_{P^{\diamond}}
=\{u:|u(-1/2)|\le1/2,\ |u(1/2)|\le1/2\}.
\]
For every such \(u\),
\[
J_{P^{\diamond}}(u)
=\frac{u(-1/2)-u(1/2)}2,
\qquad
\frac{T-J_{P^{\diamond}}(u)}A
=u(1/2)-u(-1/2).
\]
The last quantity has the attained range \([-1,1]\), so the attained-interval theorem gives \(\Theta(P^{\diamond})=[-1,1]\).

It remains to verify full-law attainment directly.  By definition,
\[
b_u^{\diamond}=
\begin{cases}
-2u(-1/2),&X=-1/2,\\
 2u(1/2),&X=1/2,
\end{cases}
\qquad
|b_u^{\diamond}|\le1.
\]
Evaluation of the schedules at the realized treatments gives
\[
Y_1^{Q_u^{\diamond}}(D_1)=0=Y_1,
\qquad
Y_2^{Q_u^{\diamond}}(D_2)=0=Y_2,
\]
so consistency holds and the entire observed law is unchanged.  For every \(d\in[-1,1]\), on the same event for all \(d\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
Y_2^{Q_u^{\diamond}}(d)-Y_1^{Q_u^{\diamond}}(d)
&=b_u^{\diamond}(D_1-D_2)\\
&=-b_u^{\diamond}Z
=u(X).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus both conditional expectations of the period difference, given \((X,Z)\) and given \(X\), equal \(u(X)\) simultaneously for every dose.  This verifies the strengthened common-event parallel-trends clause and gives \(m_{Q_u^{\diamond}}=u\).  Each schedule is individually one-Lipschitz because its slope is \(b_u^{\diamond}\).  The period-two causal movement is
\[
Y_2^{Q_u^{\diamond}}(D_2)-Y_2^{Q_u^{\diamond}}(D_1)
=b_u^{\diamond}Z=-u(X),
\]
whose conditional absolute mean is at most \(1/2=|Z|\).  Boundedness of the dose interval and the schedules gives latent integrability.  Hence every defining condition of the bounded-slope/Lipschitz sensitivity completion class holds, and
\[
\theta(Q_u^{\diamond})=u(1/2)-u(-1/2).
\]
If \(u(-1/2)=1/2\) and \(u(1/2)=-1/2\), then \(b_u^{\diamond}=-1\) at both atoms and \(\theta(Q_u^{\diamond})=-1\).  Reversing the signs gives \(b_u^{\diamond}=1\) and \(\theta(Q_u^{\diamond})=1\).  The construction uses two baseline values and opposite signs of \(Z\), so it is not the common-zero-baseline scalar design.
